info.timeAllocation:
Total Study Time: 150 hours

In-class learning: 45 hours (60 sessions)

Final exam: 1.5 hours

Self-study: 104 hours
info.studentTasks:
Students must attend at least 80% of in-class hours to be eligible for the final exam.

Actively participate in discussions and exchanges on topics presented in each lecture.

Engage in group work and complete assigned tasks effectively, contributing ideas and information to help the group fulfill its objectives.

Prepare lessons and complete assigned exercises seriously and carefully.
info.tools:
1) The instructor summarizes content, checks students’ understanding, provides lecture slides and shared files, and assigns sample exercises for practice.

2) Explore Japanese literature resources through websites suggested in the lecture slides and other relevant online sources related to the course content.

3) Refer to specialized academic materials (see the Materials file).

clos.loDetails: Acquire foundational knowledge of Japanese literature, contributing to a deeper understanding of Japan’s cultural identity through literary works

Appreciate the beauty, uniqueness, and artistic value of Japanese literature by analyzing representative works from various genres and historical periods, or by comparing similarities and differences with Vietnamese literature — supporting future research and graduation projects

Strengthen Japanese language proficiency by expanding vocabulary and expressions used in literary contexts, while deepening knowledge of Japanese society and people — enhancing the quality of thesis topics and future professional interactions with Japanese colleagues

Develop research and synthesis skills related to lecture content and assigned topics, learn how to present findings effectively, and inspire others through midterm presentations and final research projects
Cultivate teamwork, lifelong research skills, and a disciplined working style aligned with Japanese professional values

sessions.topic:
Session 33: Medieval Literature (1) 中世 – Periodization and Characteristics (genres, authors, representative works)
The Medieval period (中世) in contrast with Classical (中古) and Early Modern/Medieval-Early Modern (中世・近世).
Representative stages and genres:
(1) Wars and turmoil in the Kamakura and divided court periods: Hyakunin Isshu, Shin Kokin Wakashu, Heike Monogatari.
14th century: Travel literature (Izayoi Nikki, Towazugatari).
(2) Buddhist thought and Essays: Hojoki, Tsurezuregusa.
Uji Shui Monogatari (Setsuwa collection), development of Noh and Kyogen.
(3) Travel diaries and tales: groups of Monogatari, Medieval novels.

assessments.questionType: Analyze one or more representative authors or literary works from the selected period of Japanese literature
assessments.noQuestion:
Each class session (90 minutes) will feature two student groups presenting on topics related to literary genres and representative works from different historical periods.
Each group will present for approximately 30 minutes, followed by 15 minutes of discussion.
Presentations should address key questions such as: “Within the same genre, what are the distinctive features of this period?”
Discussion questions will vary depending on the characteristics of the genre and the historical context being presented.
assessments.knowledgeSkill:
Depending on the group’s shared interests, students may choose to explore the same literary genre across different historical periods. The focus should be on:
Identifying how the genre’s characteristics evolve over time
Highlighting similarities, differences, and new developments in each period
Selecting appropriate works and authors for analysis
Writing a presentation script and assigning roles to each member for the group report
assessments.gradingGuide:
1) Assess students’ ability to grasp key issues and understand literary genres across different historical periods
2) Evaluate language proficiency, clarity of interpretation, analytical skills, and the ability to select appropriate literary works

assessments.questionType: Research the assigned topic from the course’s exercise sequence, choose a suitable assignment type for your group, and register for the final presentation
assessments.noQuestion:
Each class session (90 minutes) may also feature two groups presenting on two literary genres and their representative works, with the same structure:
30-minute presentation
15-minute discussion
assessments.knowledgeSkill:
Each group may choose different genres, authors, or works and register their topic for presentation. While the format may vary, the core expectations include:
Expanding content beyond the textbook and lecture slides
Selecting a representative work for the chosen genre
Writing a script and assigning individual roles for the presentation
assessments.gradingGuide: Work collaboratively in groups: participate in common activities such as searching for relevant information, synthesizing information, selecting necessary content for reports, writing scripts, and engaging in group activities according to the assignments given by the group leader.
assessments.note: (Note: For the purpose of presenting midterm and final reports, students may choose to analyze the same genre (in some cases, even the same author/work), but with additional information, viewed from two different perspectives that complement and build upon each other. Therefore, students should be reminded to carefully select and register their topics for these presentations.)

assessments.note:
I. General examination organized by the examination committee\

II. Notes
1. Written assignments may be prepared in advance at home. Students are allowed to choose their preferred authors and works, in order to avoid multiple students working on the same essay (copying or borrowing from one another). They are permitted to revise their work beforehand, and during the test session they are expected to recall and write actively and independently, without cheating; this approach is intended to encourage students’ initiative and active learning.
2. While accurate grammar and writing skills are not the main focus, students must be able to express ideas clearly. Content is prioritized over form.
3. Students may cite previous studies or evaluations, but such references must be integrated into a coherent overall framework.
4. Within the allotted test time, a minimum length is required for the essay, but there is no maximum length.
5. Final exam weighting is as follows5.1 Multiple Choice: 30 minutes – 40%
5.2 Writing: 60 minutes – 60%
5.2.1 Summarizing the content of a literary work (25%)
5.2.2 Analyzing a work or excerpt from a work (35%)

III. Course completion requirements
Students must meet both of the following conditions:
a) Continuous assessment score > 0; Final exam score ≥ 4/10; Overall course score ≥ 5/10.
b) In the final exam, no skill may receive a score of 0.
